/-!
# Erdős Problem 191

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/191)
- [ErGr79] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory: van der Waerden's theorem and related topics*. Enseign. Math. (1979), 325-344.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*. (1982),
  59--79.
- [Ro03] Rödl, Vojtěch, *On homogeneous sets of positive integers*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A
  (2003), 229-240.
- [CFS13] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, *Two extensions of Ramsey's theorem*.
  Duke Math. J. (2013), 2903-2927.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos191

/--
Let $C>0$ be arbitrary. Is it true that, if $n$ is sufficiently large depending on $C$, then in
any $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ there exists some $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$
such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic and
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\geq C?$$

The answer is yes, which was proved by Rödl [Ro03]. In the same article Rödl also proved a lower
bound for this problem, constructing, for all $n$, a $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$
such that if $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$ is such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic then
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\ll \log\log\log n.$$
In the same paper Rödl proves that the answer to the main problem is negative if we consider
$3$-colourings.

This bound is best possible, as proved by Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS13], who proved that, if
$n$ is sufficiently large, then in any $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ there exists
some $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$ such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic and
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\geq 2^{-8}\log\log\log n.$$

A $2$-colouring of the pairs of $\{2,\ldots,n\}$ is a graph `G` on this vertex set; a
monochromatic set is a clique or an independent set of `G`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos191.lean#L1272"]
theorem erdos_191 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ C : ℝ, 0 < C → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Finset.Icc 2 n), ∃ X : Finset (Finset.Icc 2 n),
      (G.IsClique X ∨ G.IsIndepSet X) ∧ C ≤ ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.log (x : ℕ) := by
  sorry

/--
Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS13] proved that, if $n$ is sufficiently large, then in any
$2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ there exists some $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$ such
that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic and
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\geq 2^{-8}\log\log\log n.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_191.variants.conlon_fox_sudakov : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Finset.Icc 2 n), ∃ X : Finset (Finset.Icc 2 n),
      (G.IsClique X ∨ G.IsIndepSet X) ∧
        2 ^ (-8 : ℤ) * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n)) ≤ ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.log (x : ℕ) := by
  sorry

/--
Rödl [Ro03] constructed, for all $n$, a $2$-colouring of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ such that
if $X\subseteq \{2,\ldots,n\}$ is such that $\binom{X}{2}$ is monochromatic then
$$\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x}\ll \log\log\log n.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_191.variants.rodl_upper : ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Finset.Icc 2 n), ∀ X : Finset (Finset.Icc 2 n),
      G.IsClique X ∨ G.IsIndepSet X →
        ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.log (x : ℕ) ≤ c * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n)) := by
  sorry

/--
Rödl [Ro03] proved that the answer to [erdős_191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/191) is negative
if we consider $3$-colourings: there is a constant $C$ such that for every $n$ some $3$-colouring
of $\binom{\{2,\ldots,n\}}{2}$ has $\sum_{x\in X}\frac{1}{\log x} < C$ for every monochromatic
$X$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_191.variants.three_colours : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ,
    ∃ c : Sym2 (Finset.Icc 2 n) → Fin 3, ∀ X : Finset (Finset.Icc 2 n),
      (∃ i : Fin 3, ∀ x ∈ X, ∀ y ∈ X, x ≠ y → c s(x, y) = i) →
        ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.log (x : ℕ) < C := by
  sorry

end Erdos191

findings.description: The variant uses `Real.log` (natural log) for the weights `1 / Real.log x` and for the iterated logarithm `Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n))`. CFS13, the cited source, proves Theorem 1.1 with base-2 logarithms. With natural logs, the Lean is a strictly weaker claim than the theorem the docstring credits to CFS. The truth value is not affected in the harmful direction: I proved in Lean (scratch `cfs_implies.lean`, compiles with no sorry) that the base-2 statement `2^(-8) * logb 2 (logb 2 (logb 2 n)) ≤ ∑ 1 / logb 2 x` implies the file's natural-log statement for every n ≥ 16. So the variant is still true and `research solved` is still correct. The converse does not hold as an implication. In natural-log terms CFS's bound is 2^{-8}·log₂log₂log₂ n / ln 2 ~ 2^{-8}·(ln ln ln n)/(ln 2)² ≈ 2.08·2^{-8}·ln ln ln n. The file's constant is therefore about half of what CFS proved. The explicit constant 2^{-8} only has the stated meaning with base 2. The other declarations do not depend on the base: `C` is arbitrary, and ≪ and 'bounded' absorb constant factors. This is the only place where the base matters. erdosproblems.com copies the formula with a bare 'log', which explains the choice and makes it defensible. The repository does use `Real.logb 2` elsewhere when a source's logs are base 2 (e.g. ErdosProblems/775, 1179).
findings.source_evidence: CFS13 (arXiv:1112.1548, LaTeX source, Section 1): "All logarithms are base $2$ unless otherwise indicated." Their proof separates ln from log: "here and throughout the rest of this section we will use the natural logarithm $\ln$ as well as the log base $2$". Theorem 1.1 (erdosrodl): "For $n$ sufficiently large, every $2$-coloring of the edges of the complete graph on the interval $\{2,\ldots,n\}$ contains a monochromatic clique with vertex set $S$ such that $$\sum_{s \in S} \frac{1}{\log s} \geq 2^{-8} \log \log \log n.$$" The abstract also uses base 2 ("monochromatic clique of order $\frac{1}{2}\log n$"). erdosproblems.com/191 reproduces the formula without a base.
findings.suggested_fix: State CFS Theorem 1.1 with base-2 logs, as in the paper (this elaborates): `2 ^ (-8 : ℤ) * Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 n)) ≤ ∑ x ∈ X, 1 / Real.logb 2 (x : ℕ)`. Also say in the docstring that CFS use base-2 logarithms. Alternatively, keep `Real.log` and say in the docstring that the statement is a weaker consequence of CFS Theorem 1.1, which is stated in base 2.

reformulations.difference: The source only says that 'the answer to the main problem is negative if we consider 3-colourings'. Literally that is: ∃ C > 0 such that for infinitely many n (∃ᶠ n) some 3-colouring of the pairs of {2..n} has every monochromatic X of weight < C. The Lean states the uniform form ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n, ∃ c : Sym2 (Icc 2 n) → Fin 3, every monochromatic X has ∑ 1/log x < C. It puts no positivity on C.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Uniform ⇒ negation: take C' = max C 1 > 0. If the 3-colour analogue held for C', some n would have a monochromatic X with C' ≤ ∑ < C ≤ C', a contradiction. Negation ⇒ uniform: given m, choose n ≥ m with a good colouring c. Restrict it to {2..m} by c ∘ Sym2.map ι, where ι is the inclusion. The image under ι of a monochromatic X ⊆ {2..m} is monochromatic for c and has the same weight, so the weight is < C. So 'infinitely many n' implies 'all n', and C > 0 is automatic. This matches Rödl's actual result: the weights are uniformly bounded for every n (≤ 4 in CFS's base-2 weights, so < 6 in natural-log weights).

reformulations.difference: The Lean follows erdosproblems.com and states the finite form: ∀ C > 0, for all large n, every graph on {2..n} has a clique or independent set with ∑ 1/log x ≥ C. Erdős's original sources (ErGr79 p.333, Er81 p.15) pose the infinite form: for every 2-colouring of the pairs of positive integers, the sums ∑ 1/log x over homogeneous sets are unbounded.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finite ⇒ infinite: restrict the colouring to {2..N}. Infinite ⇒ finite: suppose the finite form fails for some C. Then for infinitely many n there is a colouring of {2..n} whose homogeneous sets all weigh < C. By restriction such a colouring exists for every n. These colourings form an infinite, finitely-branching tree under restriction, so König's lemma gives a colouring of all pairs of {2,3,...} whose finite homogeneous sets all weigh < C. The weight of an infinite homogeneous set is the supremum of its finite sub-sums, so it is ≤ C too. This contradicts the infinite form. Er81 itself says: 'Clearly it also has a finite form'.

review.notes:
Status: all four declarations are tagged `research solved`, which matches the sources. erdos_191 has answer(True); erdosproblems.com and the teorth database list the problem as 'PROVED (LEAN)'. The formal_proof link (plby/lean-proofs @8822f7d, L1272) proves `∀ C > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ G : SimpleGraph {x // x ∈ Icc 2 n}, ∃ X, (IsClique ∨ IsIndepSet) ∧ C ≤ ∑ (log x)⁻¹`. That is exactly the file's right-hand side, with no sorry.

Other checks:
- The elaborated statements (pp.coercions) are as intended: `1 / Real.log ↑↑x` with x ≥ 2, so there are no division-by-zero or negative-log junk values. `Real.log (Real.log (Real.log ↑n))` only appears under `∀ᶠ n`.
- rodl_upper: `∃ c, ∀ᶠ n` matches the erdosproblems.com definition of ≪ ('for all sufficiently large x'). Any valid c is automatically positive, since singletons have positive weight and log log log n > 0 for large n. The claim does not depend on the log base.
- Er82e states the problem on {1..n} with weights 1/(1+log i). This is equivalent to the {2..n}, 1/log x form: the weights agree up to a factor of at most 1+1/log 2, and vertex 1 contributes at most 1.
- The main docstring's phrase 'Rödl also proved a lower bound' is copied verbatim from erdosproblems.com. It is really an upper bound on f(n), as the forum comment notes, but the variant is correctly named `rodl_upper`. This does not affect the mathematics.

Access limitations:
- Direct requests to erdosproblems.com are blocked by Cloudflare, so the problem page, forum thread and definitions page were read through the r.jina.ai reader proxy.
- The full text of Rödl 2003 (ScienceDirect) was captcha-blocked. The results attributed to it — the affirmative answer, the O(log log log n) construction and the uniformly bounded 3-colour construction — were checked against three other sources: CFS13's detailed description of both constructions, Erdős 1982 (p.78), and the zbMATH review.

Lean scratch files in /workspace/review/ (none has errors):
- cfs_implies.lean: CFS's base-2 Theorem 1.1 implies the file's natural-log variant.
- three_equiv.lean: `three_colours` ↔ ¬(3-colour analogue of the main question).
- fix_check.lean: the suggested base-2 statement elaborates; a sanity check shows the main claim is trivial only for C ≤ 1/log 2.
